name: excalidraw-bridge
description: Mirrors the active editor into an Excalidraw canvas panel, and runs the program so that its output can be shown there too.

command.description: The program to run, e.g. python or node.

cwd.description: Where to run it. Defaults to the workspace root.

commands.title: Excalidraw Bridge: Show the connection details
Excalidraw Bridge: Copy the session token
Excalidraw Bridge: Open the presenter's input panel
Excalidraw Bridge: Put the presenter's window on the virtual display

excalidraw-bridge.port.description: The fixed loopback port the bridge listens on. Leave it unset: the port then comes from VITE_APP_BRIDGE_URL in the workspace's .env file - the same variable the Excalidraw page is built with - and falls back to the shared default (47511).

excalidraw-bridge.token.description: The token the Excalidraw page must present. Leave it empty and one is generated for the session. The extension NEVER ships a token: it is a secret, and the .vsix is a published artifact (D-110).

excalidraw-bridge.captureFps.description: How many frames a second the panel's live view of this editor's window takes. Six a second is enough to read by. Without the capture the panel falls back to the mirrored text and says why.

excalidraw-bridge.ocrEngine.description: The OCR engine the bridge reads with. tesseract runs in this extension's own process; indra and paddle run in a Python sidecar (see excalidraw-bridge.pythonPath).

excalidraw-bridge.pythonPath.description: The Python interpreter the indra and paddle OCR engines run in. Point it at a virtual environment that has them installed.

excalidraw-bridge.youtubeApiKey.description: Your own YouTube Data API v3 key. It is used only to read the captions of a YouTube video, and it is never sent anywhere but YouTube. Leave it empty and the captions fall back to the public endpoint, which is best effort - and the panel says which tier answered.
